title: Normalized derived global sections after pro-etale direct image
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $f:T\to Y$ and $g:Y\to W$ be morphisms of $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use the ordinary constant-$A$ module categories on small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], their bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and their direct images and exact inverse images [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Derived global sections mean the right derived evaluation at the final object; use the finite derived direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

There is a canonical natural isomorphism of functors on $D^+(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$
$$\ell_f:R\Gamma(Y,Rf_*(-))\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(T,-).$$
On a bounded-below K-injective representative $J$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex] of $L$ it is induced by the identity of section complexes $\Gamma(Y,f_*J)=\Gamma(T,J)$. This is natural for all derived morphisms, not only chain maps between specified complexes, and compatible with shifts. For the canonical direct-image composition comparison $c_{g,f}:R(gf)_*\cong Rg_*Rf_*$ [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], one has
$$\ell_{gf,L}=\ell_{f,L}\circ\ell_{g,Rf_*L}\circ R\Gamma(W,c_{g,f,L}).$$
The comparison for an identity is the identity. If $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], the composite
$$R\Gamma(T,L)\xrightarrow{R\Gamma(T,\eta_j)}R\Gamma(T,Rj_*j^*L)\xrightarrow{\ell_{j,j^*L}}R\Gamma(U,j^*L)$$
is the canonical restriction map, where $\eta_j$ is the open adjunction unit. In particular these comparisons identify derived global sections of a pushed-forward support-localization triangle with derived global sections of the original triangle, with the same third arrow and its shift comparison.
